title: kith-tslocal: Status response types
description:
Define Rust structs for Status response from Tailscale LocalAPI /localapi/v0/status.

What: Define StatusResponse in kith-tslocal/src/lib.rs with only the fields kithd needs.

Tailscale JSON field names (from real tailscale source):
- Status root: { TailscaleIPs: [netip.Addr], Self: {...}, User: {...}, BackendState: string, ... }

Algorithm:
1. Define struct StatusResponse with only fields kithd needs:
   - tailscale_ips: Vec<String>  (maps to JSON 'TailscaleIPs'; these are the listener bind IPs)
   - backend_state: String  (maps to JSON 'BackendState'; check for 'Running')
   Use #[serde(rename = 'TailscaleIPs')] on tailscale_ips.
   Use #[serde(default)] on all fields (Status may have many more fields).
2. Do NOT try to parse the full Status response - it's huge (all peer nodes).
   Use #[serde(flatten)] or ignore extra fields by using #[serde(default)] without deny_unknown.
3. All structs derive: Debug, Clone, Deserialize
4. Run: cargo test -p kith-tslocal; cargo clippy -p kith-tslocal -- -D warnings

Defensive rules:
- tailscale_ips may be empty if tailscale is not fully connected - caller must check
- Do NOT deny unknown fields (Status has dozens of fields not needed)
- backend_state='Running' is the expected healthy state; 'NeedsLogin' means not ready

Agent team: standard (R + I + T)
Tests: unit deserialization tests with hardcoded JSON.
- Test: full Status JSON parses correctly, tailscale_ips extracted
- Test: empty TailscaleIPs array parses as empty Vec (not error)
- Test: extra JSON fields ignored
Oracle: JSON fixtures hand-constructed from Tailscale LocalAPI spec.
